newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom opposes telephone price war.
newsitem.headline: Telkom opposes telephone price war.

text.p: Indonesia's PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) said on Thursday it would soon propose to the government that it does not allow a price war to develop in long distance telephone services.
"In the very short time, the board of directors will propose to the government not to allow (a) price cut," director Dadad Kustiwa told analysts in a conference call.
Telkom said in a statement the government had "set a new regulation" allowing cellular operators to build their own transmission links to provide long distance services.
Telkom said it expected to face competition, which may include price competition, from cellular operators for the provision of long distance services.
Competition and reduced interconnection and long distance revenues, could, individually or in aggregate, have a negative material impact on the company's financial performance, Telkom said.
Kustiwa, however, said he believed cellular telephone operators would use Telkom's infrastructure rather than building their own.
